topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture, introducing complement and framing the challenge of its terminology.

topics.label: Complement overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, naming conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three recognition pathways that initiate complement activation and generate surface C3 convertases to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three primary immune effector functions executed upon complement activation: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host tissues
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from non-specific complement activation and damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes caused by genetic or acquired deficiencies in complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to evade complement destruction, highlighting mechanisms and applications of Staphylococcus aureus proteins.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and announces the topic of the upcoming lecture.
